accuracy: not established: the checked stopping equation has no bounded physical remainder in this record; binding-expansion, omitted recoil, finite-size and bound-state radiative contributions remain unbounded. The independent point-Coulomb reference omits physical corrections and its abstract was exposed before the budget was fixed; the interpretation remains provisional
interpretation: The primary equations and the independent point-Coulomb comparison inform this provisional interpretation; they do not establish physical accuracy. No nuclide is admitted.

references.citation: A. Czarnecki, A. O. Davydov and M. Y. Kaygorodov, Total decay rate of a muon bound to a light nucleus, Phys. Rev. D 113, 036028 (2026)
references.comparison: Table I and equations (14)-(15); the Geant4 ratio is to its free-rate parameter whereas the reference normalizes to the massless-electron free width. Literal and electron-mass-normalized comparisons have different outcomes for a residual-scaling prediction. No final interpretation is adopted.
references.exposure: its abstract-level conclusion (the (alpha Z)^2/2 leading term is confirmed, and an earlier oxygen value is attributed to a partial-wave series that had not converged) was read before the budget was fixed; no tabulated value was
references.scope: Gamma/Gamma0 for a 1s muon in a static point Coulomb potential, Z = 4 to 9, computed with its own partial-wave code; finite size, screening, radiative and recoil corrections are not included

sources.citation: H. C. von Baeyer and D. Leiter, Nuclear recoil corrections to the lifetime of bound muons, Phys. Rev. A 19, 1371 (1979)
sources.role: equation (30), pp. 1373-1374: the stopping expression through (Z alpha)^2 and (Z alpha)^2 m/M; point nucleus and massless electron; validity stated qualitatively

sources.citation: N. C. Mukhopadhyay, Nuclear muon capture, Phys. Rep. 30, 1 (1977)
sources.role: section 2.2, p. 9, equation (2.9): qualitative phase-space term with coefficient about 2.5 and nuclear charge Z; compare the complete leading coefficient in von Baeyer and Leiter, equation (27)

sources.citation: R. W. Huff, Decay rate of bound muons, Ann. Phys. 16, 288 (1961)
sources.role: Table II: computed total rates for Fe, Sb, Pb and U

sources.citation: P. Haenggi, R. D. Viollier, U. Raff and K. Alder, Muon decay in orbit, Phys. Lett. B 51, 119 (1974)
sources.role: pp. 119-122: spectra including finite size and vacuum polarization

sources.citation: A. Czarnecki, M. Dowling, X. Garcia i Tormo, W. J. Marciano and R. Szafron, Michel decay spectrum for a muon bound to a nucleus, Phys. Rev. D 90, 093002 (2014)
sources.role: context only: it describes the binding effects on the total decay rate as approximately cancelling, the difference from the free rate being mainly time dilation, and its convolution formula neither covers the high-energy end of the spectrum nor includes all corrections of order (Z alpha)^2, so it bounds no term of the total rate

binding_expansion.note: No bound is assigned in this record to terms beyond the orders retained in equation (30).

equation.statement: Gamma_bound/Gamma_free = 1 - (1/2)(Z alpha)^2 - 0.06 (Z alpha)^2 m_mu/M, M the nuclear mass; Geant4's expression below Z = 14 is this equation

finite_size.note: No bound is assigned in this record to the low-Z finite-size contribution to the inclusive total width.

nuclear_mass.source: von Baeyer and Leiter (1979), equation (30): conditional propagation only, assuming relative nuclear-mass error at most 1/2; this assumption is not an uncertainty measurement

numerical.source: closed-form binary64 evaluation checked by bound_rates_oracle in cpp/test/CMakeLists.txt, implemented in cpp/test/bound_rate_check.cc; implementation agreement only, not a bound on physical omitted terms

radiative.note: No bound is assigned here to bound-state radiative corrections to the inclusive total width.

recoil.note: Omitted recoil orders are unbounded in this record; only the term in equation (30) is included.
